value: Second Amended and Restated Credit Agreement
agreement_text_basis: Agreement dated July 2 2026 among Sterling Infrastructure Inc.; guarantors from time to time; lenders from time to time; and BMO Bank N.A. as Administrative Agent.
what_it_proves: Moves Sterling from source-locator/filed-summary to actual agreement-text evidence.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not by itself prove how much was drawn or which projects used the facility.
next_source: Sterling borrowing notices, Q3/Q4 2026 debt roll-forward, and cash-flow statements

agreement_section: Definition of Revolving Credit Commitment and Schedule 1
agreement_text_basis: Borrower and lenders acknowledge Revolving Credit Commitments aggregate 1.500B USD as of closing; Schedule 1 lender commitments total 1.500B USD.
what_it_proves: Confirms the July 2026 platform reset is a legally committed lender facility, not only management presentation language.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove availability after L/Cs, reserves, defaults, or borrowing conditions.
next_source: Availability disclosures and compliance certificates

agreement_section: Definition of Revolving Credit Termination Date
agreement_text_basis: Revolving Credit Termination Date means July 2 2031 or earlier termination under the agreement.
what_it_proves: Confirms the credit wrapper is a five-year committed platform from July 2026 to July 2031.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove debt will remain outstanding or undrawn through maturity.
next_source: Future debt maturity table and amendments

term_metric: Revolving loans may be repaid and reborrowed
agreement_text_basis: Section 2.2 states revolving loans may be repaid and principal amounts reborrowed before the Revolving Credit Termination Date.
what_it_proves: Supports the hypothesis that Sterling needed flexible platform liquidity rather than one-time fixed project debt.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not identify the actual draw pattern or working-capital timing.
next_source: Quarterly revolver balance and operating working-capital bridge

agreement_section: Definition of L/C Sublimit and Section 2.3
agreement_text_basis: L/C Sublimit means 600M USD; letters of credit are part of the revolving credit and constitute usage of lender commitments.
what_it_proves: Shows the revolver is also a guarantee/bonding-style support tool relevant to project/backlog execution.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not show actual outstanding letters of credit, beneficiaries, or project-level guarantees.
next_source: L/C outstanding disclosures, surety/bonding notes, and backlog contract terms

agreement_section: Definition of Swing Line Sublimit and Section 2.7
agreement_text_basis: Swing Line Sublimit means 50M USD; Section 2.7 permits swing loans that may be repaid and used again before the termination date.
what_it_proves: Adds short-term liquidity mechanics inside the revolver for working-capital timing.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove swing-line usage or daily cash needs.
next_source: Cash management disclosures and revolver activity

agreement_text_basis: Applicable Margin grid: SOFR loans and letter-of-credit fee range from 1.25% at Total Net Leverage Ratio below 1.00x to 2.00% at 3.00x or higher; performance L/C fees are 67% of applicable rates.
what_it_proves: Turns the prior pricing clue into actual spread economics tied to leverage.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not provide Sterling's actual quarter-end pricing level without the leverage calculation and pricing date.
next_source: Compliance certificates and debt-interest footnotes

agreement_text_basis: Applicable Margin grid: Base Rate loans and reimbursement obligations range from 0.25% to 1.00% depending on Total Net Leverage Ratio.
what_it_proves: Shows Sterling's cost of capital is explicitly leverage-sensitive.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove actual borrowing mix between Base Rate and SOFR loans.
next_source: Borrowing notices and interest expense reconciliation

agreement_section: Definition of Applicable Margin and Section 2.12
agreement_text_basis: Applicable Margin grid sets commitment fee from 0.15% to 0.25%; Section 2.12 charges commitment fee on average daily unused revolving commitments.
what_it_proves: Shows Sterling pays for unused committed flexibility, which fits the platform-liquidity hypothesis.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not tell how much unused capacity remained after borrowings and L/Cs.
next_source: Quarterly unused commitment and fee expense disclosures

agreement_text_basis: Proceeds may be used to refinance existing indebtedness, finance certain capital expenditures, general working capital, Permitted Acquisitions, other general corporate purposes, prepay Existing Term Loans, fund related fees and expenses, and other legal/proper purposes consistent with applicable laws.
what_it_proves: Directly supports the hypothesis that Sterling's facility is a flexible funding wrapper for refinancing, capex, working capital, and acquisitions.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove any specific dollar went to a specific acquisition, capex project, or backlog job.
next_source: Post-close debt roll-forward, acquisition funding note, and capex cash-flow schedule

agreement_section: Definition of Available Incremental Amount and Section 2.18
agreement_text_basis: Available Incremental Amount includes the greater of 500M USD and 100% of EBITDA, plus an unlimited amount if pro forma Total Net Leverage Ratio is less than or equal to 2.00x under specified assumptions.
what_it_proves: Shows the agreement contains a growth/acquisition expansion mechanism beyond the headline 1.5B USD revolver.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove Sterling can satisfy the pro forma leverage test at any future acquisition date.
next_source: Pro forma leverage calculations and acquisition financing disclosures

agreement_text_basis: Material Acquisition means a Permitted Acquisition having Total Consideration in excess of 250M USD; Permitted Acquisitions require no default and pro forma compliance with financial covenants plus leverage cushion rules.
what_it_proves: Shows acquisitions are contemplated but covenant-gated, which is exactly the platform funding question.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove a future deal will qualify or be debt-funded.
next_source: Acquisition announcements, purchase agreements, and compliance certificates

agreement_text_basis: Borrower shall not permit Total Net Leverage Ratio to be greater than 3.50 to 1.00 as of each fiscal-quarter end.
what_it_proves: Adds the actual leverage ceiling that was missing from filed-summary evidence.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not provide current covenant cushion without EBITDA, debt, and unrestricted cash calculation.
next_source: Compliance certificate Schedule I

agreement_text_basis: Borrower may elect up to two covenant holiday periods during the term to increase maximum Total Net Leverage Ratio to 4.00x for four fiscal quarters in connection with a Material Acquisition, subject to conditions and spacing.
what_it_proves: Shows the agreement is explicitly designed to flex around material acquisitions.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not prove management will use the holiday or that acquisitions will create value.
next_source: Acquisition financing events and covenant election notices

agreement_text_basis: Borrower shall maintain Interest Coverage Ratio of not less than 3.00 to 1.00 as of each fiscal-quarter end.
what_it_proves: Adds the second core financial covenant and a downside cash-flow discipline test.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not provide actual covenant cushion without cash interest and EBITDA calculations.
next_source: Compliance certificate Schedule I and interest expense footnote

agreement_section: Definition of Total Net Leverage Ratio
agreement_text_basis: Total Net Leverage Ratio nets unrestricted cash only up to an amount equal to 50% of EBITDA for the four fiscal-quarter period.
what_it_proves: Shows the leverage covenant is not a simple gross-debt ratio; cash netting is allowed but capped.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not compute actual net leverage.
next_source: Compliance certificate Schedule I

agreement_text_basis: Obligations shall be guaranteed by each direct and indirect subsidiary other than excluded subsidiaries; signature pages include multiple named guarantors including CEC Facilities LLC and Stone Ridge Infrastructure LLC.
what_it_proves: Shows the credit wrapper reaches operating subsidiaries and acquired entities, not only parent-level credit.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not map each project or customer contract to a guarantor.
next_source: Subsidiary schedule and collateral documents

value: all personal property of borrower and guarantors
agreement_text_basis: Obligations are secured by valid perfected enforceable liens on all right title and interest of Borrower and each Guarantor in all personal property, subject to Section 11.29 and collateral documents.
what_it_proves: Confirms the revolver is secured by broad personal-property collateral, supporting the credit-wrapper hypothesis.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not quantify collateral value, priority exceptions, excluded assets, or borrowing availability.
next_source: Collateral documents, UCC filings, and lender collateral schedules

agreement_section: Definition of Excluded Subsidiary and Section 7.3(m)
term_metric: Project Specific JV exclusion and investment basket
agreement_text_basis: Excluded subsidiaries include Project Specific JVs; investments in Project Specific JVs are permitted up to greater of 360M USD and 30% of Net Worth outstanding at any time, calculated net of distributions.
what_it_proves: Adds nuance: some project-specific structures may sit outside the main guarantor/collateral package.
what_it_does_not_prove: Does not identify which backlog projects are in excluded JVs or how customer funding flows through them.
next_source: Project JV agreements and backlog/customer schedules

agreement_text_basis: The actual agreement supports the hypothesis that Sterling's funding container is a flexible secured platform revolver with L/C, swing-line, acquisition, capex, refinancing, covenant, guaranty, and collateral mechanics.
what_it_proves: Sterling can be described as agreement-term-visible for the credit wrapper.
what_it_does_not_prove: It still cannot be described as project-source-of-funds-grade or customer-funded-backlog-proof.
next_source: Sterling backlog contract funding pass and covenant-cushion pass
